hook.line: When someone is upset about something small, the kindest thing you can say is that it isn't worth it. Spanish says you *give* a thing importance, and you can choose not to.
hook.es: No le des importancia, fue un malentendido.
hook.en: Don't make a big deal of it, it was a misunderstanding. (to a friend)

examples.es: No le des importancia, fue un malentendido.
examples.en: Don't make a big deal of it, it was a misunderstanding. (to a friend)

examples.en: You attach too much importance to what people say. (to a friend)

examples.en: Vale didn't make a big deal of the comment.

examples.en: Don't make such a big deal of the fight. (to a friend)

rule:
To make something matter, you *give* it importance: *darle importancia a algo*. Most often it is a calming command: *No le des importancia*. Without *no*, it is a gentle complaint: *le das demasiada importancia*.

*Le* always stays, even when you name the thing: *le das importancia a lo que dice la gente*.

To say something does or doesn't matter, use *tener*: *no tiene importancia*, *tiene mucha importancia*.

Lighter options: *no pasa nada*, *no importa*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *le* here a doubled indirect object pronoun, and *no le des* a negative command. Both are standard.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *des* or *das* and type the whole sentence, a calming command to a friend: *No le ___ importancia, fue un malentendido.*
yourTurn.answer: No le des importancia, fue un malentendido.
yourTurn.why: A 'don't' to a friend uses *des*; *das* would be a statement.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: That doesn't matter.
yourTurn.why: To say something matters or doesn't, use *tener importancia*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Don't make such a big deal of the fight. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No le des tanta importancia a la pelea.
yourTurn.why: *Tanta* goes right before *importancia*, and *a* introduces the thing you are making a fuss about.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You attach too much importance to what people say. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Le das demasiada importancia a lo que dice la gente.
yourTurn.why: *Demasiada* agrees with *importancia*, and *le* stays even though the thing is named.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a stranger, formal: Don't make a big deal of it, ma'am.
yourTurn.why: With *usted*, the command is *dé*, with an accent, instead of *des*.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it in the past: *Vale no le da importancia al comentario.* Say: Vale didn't make a big deal of the comment.
yourTurn.answer: Vale no le dio importancia al comentario.
yourTurn.why: *Dio* is the past of *da*, and *le* stays in place.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It matters a lot to me that you tell me the truth. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Para mí tiene mucha importancia que me digas la verdad.
yourTurn.why: *Tiene mucha importancia* says it matters, and *digas* is the wish form after *que*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Keep the little word *le*: you give importance *to it*.
As a 'don't' to a friend, the verb takes *des*, not *das*.
After *tener* you need the noun *importancia*; *importante* is the adjective.

pitfalls.wrong: No le des importancia de lo que dije.
pitfalls.right: No le des importancia a lo que dije.
pitfalls.why: You give importance *a* something, not *de* it.

personal: Think of something small that bothered you this week and tell yourself to let it go: *No le des importancia a ...*
